arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: General Garre argued the FCC acted to fulfill its statutory mandate to protect children from indecent content.
He cited the Commission's acknowledgment of a policy change in the relevant order to support the agency's position.
Justice Stevens questioned whether the specific word in question carries a sexual connotation in all contexts.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the limits of government power to regulate speech in the home. It determines whether broadcasters face strict liability for brief, accidental profanity during live events. The outcome shapes the balance between parental protection and free expression on television.
